t: Minimum Deletions for At Most K Distinct Characters
o: Delete characters so at most k distinct letters remain, minimizing deletions. Clearly we keep the k most frequent characters and delete everything else. Count frequencies (<= 26 distinct), sort descending, keep the top k, and sum the rest. Example 3: frequencies y=3, z=2, k=1 keeps y and deletes 2.
k: Optimal strategy: retain the k highest-frequency characters, delete all occurrences of the rest.
At most 26 distinct letters, so counting + sorting is trivial.

a.i: Tally character counts, sort descending, and delete every occurrence outside the top k.
s: Answer = sum of counts beyond index k-1.

w: Straightforward greedy; the exchange argument (swapping a kept rare letter for a deleted frequent one never helps) proves optimality. Edge cases: k >= number of distinct letters gives 0.
